newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kizu seeks insolvency of two borrowers -- Teikoku.
newsitem.headline: Kizu seeks insolvency of two borrowers -- Teikoku.

text.p: Failed credit union Kizu Shinyo Kumiai applied last week to Osaka District Court for two of its 10 largest borrowers to be declared insolvent, private credit research firm Teikoku Databank Ltd said on Tuesday.
A spokesman for Osaka District Court on Tuesday declined to confirm whether Kizu had made such applications.
Teikoku Databank said the two companies that were the subject of the application were Marutaka KK, an Osaka-based real estate developer, and Iwai Kensetsu KK, a construction company in Osaka.
Teikoku said Marutaka's outstanding debts totalled 60.1 billion yen and Iwai Kensetsu's 27 billion yen.
A spokesman for Marutaka was not immediately available.
An Iwai Kensetsu official confirmed that Kizu had filed with the court for the firm's insolvency, but said its total debts were 23 billion yen.
Kizu, an Osaka-based credit union, collapsed in 1995.
